description:
Holly (Ilex spp.) includes many shrubs and trees with glossy leaves and bright berries. It is toxic to cats, and the berries are often the easiest part for a cat to find or swallow.

Holly contains saponins and other irritating compounds. These can upset the stomach and intestines. The sharp leaves can also irritate the mouth, while fallen berries may attract curious cats during the holiday season.

A cat that eats holly may drool, vomit, have diarrhea, smack the lips, or seem uncomfortable. Keep holly decorations and outdoor berries away from cats. Call a veterinarian if your cat eats several berries, vomits repeatedly, or seems weak.
name: Ilex

symptoms.name: Vomiting and Diarrhea
symptoms.onset: Acute (Clinical signs can occur after ingesting as few as two berries).

symptoms.name: Head Shaking or Pawing at Mouth
